instruction: Change Chrome's default search engine to DuckDuckGo.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened Chrome and tried to navigate to google.com/preferences to change search results per page. Hit SSL certificate errors (NET::ERR_CERT_COMMON_NAME_INVALID) due to proxy. Spent 50 turns trying curl, terminal debugging, and various URL attempts. Never declared the task as infeasible.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome from desktop, type URLs in address bar, use keyboard shortcuts (Enter, F5), open and use terminal, interact with Chrome UI elements (buttons, address bar)
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed on two fronts: (1) SSL cert errors prevented accessing google.com through the proxy, (2) never recognized the task was infeasible. Model exhausted all 50 turns without declaring [INFEASIBLE].
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to a Chrome local settings task (search engine change via chrome://settings/searchEngines) that doesn't require internet access and is closely related to the original task's theme of modifying search settings.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating to Chrome search engine settings and changing the default to DuckDuckGo. Evaluator uses existing default_search_engine getter to read Chrome's search provider from preferences and custom check_search_engine metric for case-insensitive string comparison.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter 'default_search_engine' correctly reads Chrome's Preferences JSON and extracts 'default_search_provider_data.template_url_data.short_name', which is the exact state needed to verify the default search engine.
Metric correctly handles the 'type: rule' pattern by accessing 'expected.get("expected_engine")' directly from the rules dict, avoiding the common anti-pattern of trying to unwrap a 'rules' key.
Case-insensitive string comparison is appropriate for search engine name matching (e.g., 'duckduckgo' vs 'DuckDuckGo').
Full coverage: the single instruction requirement (change default search engine to DuckDuckGo) is completely verified by the evaluator.
Error handling is present: the metric checks for error strings in the result and returns 0.0 appropriately.
